crosswalks.label: Maintenance and Repair Workers, General
crosswalks.rationale: O*NET includes Maintenance Engineer as a sample reported title and exposes relevant physical maintenance work, but the occupation is broader/general and not equivalent to engineering-level maintenance responsibility across industries.

crosswalks.label: General Maintenance and Repair Workers
crosswalks.rationale: The BLS profile provides useful public-domain evidence on physical duties, tools, work environment, recordkeeping and escalation to licensed trades but represents general maintenance work rather than every Maintenance Engineer role.

crosswalks.label: Petroleum, petrochemical and natural gas industries — Collection and exchange of reliability and maintenance data for equipment
crosswalks.rationale: The standard is sector-specific reliability/maintenance-data context already referenced by the body; under the source policy its copyrighted text remains reference-only and does not define universal maintenance practice.

findings.summary: Public occupation evidence supports preventive maintenance, inspection/testing, diagnosis, repair and detailed work records as recurring maintenance work.
findings.rationale: The body already reconstructs preventive/predictive/corrective strategy, failure analysis, work planning, history and restoration verification.

findings.summary: Human maintenance work uses hand/power tools, precision/electrical measuring instruments, installation/setup, alignment, balancing and direct physical inspection/repair actions.
findings.rationale: The current body deliberately protects physical/safety boundaries but mostly models analysis/planning; it does not yet reconstruct the physical tool classes, inspection interfaces and execution handoff deeply enough for machines/robots/humans to share the same professional package.

findings.summary: Maintenance work includes ordering/requisitioning parts and supplies, making spares identification, compatibility and work-order linkage part of the real workflow.
findings.rationale: The body mentions spares/resources in work planning but lacks a first-class parts/spares provenance and compatibility tool contract.

findings.summary: Occupational evidence includes reading blueprints, repair manuals, parts catalogs and diagrams to plan and execute maintenance.
findings.rationale: The body retrieves OEM/site procedures but should represent versioned drawings/diagrams/catalogs and exact asset/configuration applicability explicitly.

findings.summary: General maintenance workers are expected to recognize work beyond their skills/authorization and route specialized tasks to licensed trades such as electricians/plumbers/HVAC specialists.
findings.rationale: The body escalates to Safety/OEM/Specialist Engineer but does not explicitly reconstruct trade/licensing boundaries that can determine who may execute physical work.

findings.summary: Maintenance work can involve ladders, tight spaces, heat/cold and other physical hazards, so real execution depends on site conditions beyond abstract asset state.
findings.rationale: The body has strong hazard-stop language but needs a richer work-environment/context interface before physical execution can ever be safely composed.

gaps_against_body.description: Research physical inspection, measurement, hand/power-tool and installation/alignment/balancing work into a separate execution map with explicit human/robot/tool capabilities and hard safety authorization stops.
Add parts/spares identification, compatibility, inventory/procurement handoff and work-order provenance without allowing an automated package to substitute a part solely from similarity.
Add versioned drawing/manual/diagram/catalog retrieval tied to exact asset configuration so stale or wrong-model technical documents cannot silently drive work.
Add explicit licensed-trade/site-role routing for work whose execution authority or competence is outside the current maintenance executor.

contradictions.description: O*NET reports Maintenance Engineer as a sample title inside a general maintenance occupation, but that does not establish equivalence with engineering-level maintenance roles; the mapping remains partial.

nonclaims: This packet does not establish that O*NET 49-9071.00 is equivalent to Maintenance Engineer across industries.
ISO 14224 standard text is not ingested or reproduced; only public metadata/reference status is used under the research source policy.
No physical inspection, tool operation, isolation, permit, energization, repair authorization, licensed-trade authority or return-to-service certification is granted by this research.
A machine or model may analyze maintenance evidence but may not claim physical observations it did not perform.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: This research packet grants no authority to isolate, energize, open, repair, test, return to service, or otherwise intervene on physical equipment; site/OEM/regulatory permits, competent-person roles and direct physical evidence remain external gates.
